lens_summary: Kaggle intel without Kaggle access (kaggle.com blocked here: one curl to the Kaggle API returned 000; WebSearch indexes Kaggle pages by title only, with no LB snippets). GitHub mirrors of other teams (JunhaoLiXD 0.942/0.944, alvaromendizabal 0.947, Kai-Gowers 0.927, Gluzdov 0.926, sota1111, davidlueng986, kito2718) contain NOTHING above 0.953 and no top-team method; searches for top names (Sergio Alvarez, yu4u, Tang, tatsutaka) and Japanese/X posts found nothing. New facts from this pass: (a) Kai-Gowers' reports show the public pilkwang primary was trained 400 epochs (epoch 381 picked on leaky val) on 4xL40S for ~2 days per seed, and a 179-video retrain with the same recipe scored 0.927 vs 0.942. A detector retrain like the top teams' cannot be done by 29 Sep, which matches the BRIEF. Public RETRAINED weights (georgexue666 pool-2/sigma-0.8, CC0) are the only feasible stand-in for a 'model improvement'. (b) Reading the x138 source (experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb) turned up a runtime guard that nobody on our side has audited. REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=27000 s is counted from kernel start. After 7.5 h, every remaining movie is post-processed without relink, gap closing, gap2, safe divisions or linefit. The repair loop runs after ALL GPU prediction, in sorted file order. Our own hidden-test runs of the same GPU stack take ~7.5 h end to end (#31: 17:09 -> 00:39), so x138 may cross its own guard. If so, the last movies in sorted order (possibly the whole private embryo) lose ~0.04-0.05 each. That is a finals risk and an edge over the 41 teams running x138 verbatim. (c) x138's readmit/gapfill nodes come from an unrefined int16 lattice dump, so they miss the head shift. (d) thtennant's private 0.959 was most likely built WITHOUT V1284: the head dataset was private until 24 Sep 03:04 and he is a separate team. His chain therefore likely holds another non-public lever, and his notebooks' version histories should be read. Honest ceiling of this lens: every idea here is worth 0 to +0.006 on public in expectation (sum of expectations ~+0.003-0.004). The only large number is the private insurance of the runtime-guard fix (up to +0.02 private if the guard fires). Realistic public landing: ~0.953-0.958. 0.99 is unreachable: it is 0.015 above the current #1 (0.975), and all disclosed top-team gains come from multi-day model retraining. On the user's Kaggle-API offer: the key would NOT help this container, because kaggle.com is blocked at the network level. It helps on friend A's PC or the user's laptop, for example `kaggle kernels output vitaliineibauer/biohub-exp56-x138-verbatim -p out56` (dummy log with per-movie timings), `kaggle kernels list --competition biohub-cell-tracking-during-development --sort-by dateRun` and `kaggle kernels pull <ref> -m`. hypotheses.title: Audit and lift x138's 7.5 h repair deadline so the last hidden movies keep relink, gaps, safe divisions and linefit
hypotheses.mechanism: x138 sets BIOHUB_REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=27000, counted from BIOHUB_KERNEL_START_TS (cell 0). The repair loop write_test_submission() starts only after GPU prediction and the ILP have finished for every hidden movie, and it walks the geffs in sorted path order (cell 5). The first movie whose repair starts after 7.5 h calls _deadline_degrade(). From then on OUTPUT_MOTION_RELINK, OUTPUT_GAP_CLOSE, OUTPUT_GAP2_RECOVERY, OUTPUT_SAFE_DIVISIONS and OUTPUT_LINEFIT_SMOOTH are False for all remaining movies ('edge filtering and short-track filtering only'). Our hidden runs of the SAME GPU stack (exp51: same models, TTA and head) take ~7.5 h from submit to score (#31 17:09 -> 00:39 UTC; CONTEXT.md). x138's tail (flow relink twice, readmit, gapfill) is in the same cost class. So x138 plausibly crosses its own guard near the end of the loop. The degraded block is a contiguous run of the alphabetically last movies, plausibly all of one embryo, so it can hit the private 71% while leaving public intact. Cost per degraded movie on the LB: safe divisions off -0.036 (probe 26); relink off -0.002 (probe 21); linefit +0.0145 in the lab (B28); gap closing +0.004 in the lab (RESULTS exp07+pp). That is roughly -0.04..-0.05 of score per degraded movie (a guess built from these numbers). Lifting the deadline to ~10 h costs nothing when the run is fast and recovers the tail when it is not.
hypotheses.change: On the F1 base (exp56 = x138, or exp57b if #35 > #34), change ONE env value in cell 0: BIOHUB_REPAIR_DEADLINE_S 27000 -> 36000 (10 h). Optional second step (only after reading the dummy log's stage timings): keep linefit and safe divisions in _deadline_degrade(), because they are cheap per movie and worth ~0.05 together, and switch off only the relink/gap stages. Add a projected-finish print: elapsed + remaining_movies x max(repair_s so far) against 11.3 h. Implementation: tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 currently allows only divinsert|leafprune, so add a '--set KEY=VALUE' passthrough for cell-0 env knobs. The dummy run must produce a CSV that is byte-identical to the base, because the 4 dummy movies finish in minutes.

hypotheses.upper_bound: Let f be the fraction of hidden GT-edge weight in degraded movies and L ~0.045 the per-movie loss (guess from -0.036 divisions, -0.002 relink, ~-0.01 linefit after an LB discount, -0.004 gaps). The total-score loss is ~L x f. Public ceiling if the degraded block is inside the public embryo: L x f/0.29, i.e. +0.015 at f = 0.1. Private ceiling: L x f/0.71, i.e. +0.006 at f = 0.1 and +0.019 at f = 0.3. If the guard never fires the gain is exactly 0: output is byte-identical because the code path is unchanged.
hypotheses.expected_public_gain: E ~ +0.001 (range 0 to +0.015): P(guard fires on the hidden run) ~0.35 (guess) x P(the degraded block includes public movies | fires) ~0.3 x ~+0.01 = ~+0.001.
hypotheses.expected_private_gain: E ~ +0.0015-0.002 (range 0 to +0.02): 0.35 x 0.7 x ~+0.006-0.008 at f ~0.1. This is mostly insurance for the finals and an edge over the 41 verbatim x138 copies.
hypotheses.probability: ~0.35 that the guard fires at all on the hidden run (guess). Arithmetic: exp51 (same GPU phase) needs ~7.5 h end to end; x138's tail is at least as heavy; so the 7.5 h mark falls inside the repair loop. The alternative is a GPU phase much shorter than latency suggests: latency includes queueing, and Kaggle may run the hidden set faster. P(no harm) ~0.98, if the 10 h limit keeps >= 1.5 h of margin.
hypotheses.validation_protocol: Pre-registered: (1) From the exp56 dummy log (browser_todo item 2), compute GPU+ILP seconds per movie and repair seconds per movie without setup, then project to 100 and 130 movies. The fix is URGENT if the projected repair start exceeds 6.5 h or the projected end exceeds 7.5 h. (2) Compare #34's latency (browser_todo item 1) with #31's. If #34 takes >= 30 min longer, raise the priority. (3) Dummy run of the patched kernel: CSV sha256 identical to exp56 (or exp57b), no 'DEADLINE:' line, and the projected-finish print present. (4) LB rule: public >= base -> adopt the deadline change into BOTH finals (it cannot hurt a run that finishes in time). Public >= base + 0.003 -> the guard WAS firing on public movies. A tie is inconclusive for private but the change is still adopted. No in-sample lab is involved: the change touches no model and no geometry.

hypotheses.title: Use the public retrained precision detector (georgexue666 pool-2, sigma 0.8 um, CC0) as a second localiser and readmit source on the x138 stack
hypotheses.mechanism: The loss is a node-POSITION problem. About 2,700 swap/diverted FN come from annotated nuclei that sit between two of our tracks (oracle +0.03-0.046). The 1,907 a_never FN have their nearest raw peak at a median of 8.65 um, i.e. just outside the 7 um gate (edge anatomy; wf_ideas_v2 r1_hyp_detection). The V1284 head, a 10% centre-error cut from frozen coarse features, gave +0.007 on the x138 base because x138's tail consumes positions. Top teams say their gains came from retraining the detector, which we cannot do by 29 Sep (400-epoch reference). A retrained detector is, however, public. georgexue666's UNet heatmap detector has twice the xy resolution of the public grid (pool=2) and a tight 0.8 um Gaussian trained directly on Kaggle GT. Its peaks therefore follow the ANNOTATION convention at finer resolution. Two uses: (a) localiser: move each x138 node toward the nearest precision peak within r (1.5-2 um), weighted, i.e. an independent second estimate of the same nucleus centre; (b) readmit source: precision peaks > 5 um from every node and within 4 um of an open track end are re-admitted the way x138 already readmits its own peaks. This targets under-segmentation in dense regions, which the sigma-0.8 map separates better. Neither use swaps the node set wholesale, which is the secondary-swap class closed on the LB.
hypotheses.change: (1) Browser: dataset files, README, model code, D1.json (browser_todo item 7). (2) Friend A: run the model on the 32 D1-VAL movies (out-of-sample for it) and dump peaks. On CPU, compare against GT: for every annotated node, the distance to (i) the V1284-refined public peak (public head applied to our 199 captures, experiments/coordhead_retrain), (ii) the fused position for r in {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} um and weights w in {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}; also count the 7 um matches. (3) If the gate passes: a kernel patch after the V1284 refine in the predict script (x138 cell 4). The precision UNet runs once per frame without TTA on the GPU shard, fused positions replace arr before coord_offset, and variant (b) extends the readmit pool. Plus the runtime-guard fix.

The V1284 shift alone carries exp51's gain (exp54 zero-mode CSV byte-identical to exp48), +0.007 on the x138 base and +0.002 on ours.

The 1,907 a_never FN come from 1,567 GT nodes whose nearest raw peak is at a median of 8.65 um; 424 have no peak within 10 um.
The reference primary was trained 400 epochs, ~2 days per seed on 4xL40S. Retraining is out of reach.
Tang (3rd): most of the gain comes from model improvements; the public ckpt 'hit a wall'.

hypotheses.title: Rider: apply the V1284 head to x138's low-detection pool so readmitted and gap-filled nodes get refined, float positions
hypotheses.mechanism: In x138 the low-detection dump (peaks >= 0.3 feeding readmit and gapfill) is taken from _detect_cells_pooled before _v1284_refine, scaled to full resolution and cast to int16 ('lowdet write'). readmit_discarded_detections then inserts these raw lattice positions as nodes, and gapfill bridges through them. So the ~1.1% of nodes that readmit adds (1,337 of 121,777 on the dummy clips), plus up to 3% from gapfill, miss the head's median ~0.4-0.7 um shift toward the annotation convention (mean shift 0.74 um on the main peaks). They also carry the 1.625 um z lattice. These nodes sit at track ends and inside gaps, exactly where the swap/diverted errors live. The same head applied to them removes an inconsistency inside the stack that made the head pay (+0.007 on x138).
hypotheses.change: In the x138 predict-script patch (cell 4 'lowdet peaks'), compute the scores at the integer peaks first (as now). Then apply _low = _v1284_refine(ds_path, t, _low, unet_out[:, f_idx]) (the same head, same features; the refine function already handles any peak array) and store _lc as float32 without the int16 cast. The readmit and gapfill code already reads low_coords as float64 (cell 5 load_low_detections). Guard it with a knob LOWDET_REFINE=0|1; 0 must be byte-identical to x138.

evidence.claim: lowdet is dumped before refinement and cast to int16.
Readmit inserts peaks['vox'] positions directly as nodes; load_low_detections reads low_coords as float64.
1,337 readmitted nodes over 4 dummy clips (121,777 raw nodes); leaf prune removed 479 readmitted leaves (they are fragile track ends).
Head shift on the main peaks: mean 0.739 um, max 1.61 um.

hypotheses.upper_bound: If readmit/gapfill nodes (~2-4% of nodes, but concentrated at track ends) got the same benefit per node as the head gave overall (+0.007 for 100% of nodes on x138), the ceiling is ~0.03 x 0.007 = +0.0002..+0.0003, x2-3 for their end-of-track position: ~+0.001 at most.
hypotheses.expected_public_gain: +0.0003 (range 0 to +0.001). Invisible on the LB alone; ride it with runtime-guard-audit.
hypotheses.probability: 0.6 that it is non-negative. It is the same learned shift applied to peaks of the same detector.
hypotheses.validation_protocol: Dummy-run checks: (1) with LOWDET_REFINE=0 the CSV is byte-identical to the base; (2) with 1, the main (non-readmitted) node set and ILP counts are identical, readmitted counts change by < 10%, and the shift stats of the lowdet peaks resemble the main peaks (mean ~0.7 um, max < 2 um). If friend A's x138 lab cache exists, replay the tail with and without it and report J per embryo, trusting only the sign. No separate LB slot: it rides in the runtime-guard probe, where both parts are expected to be non-negative.
